note: Operational signals, not a billing statement.
prune_policy: Do not run broad workspace scans without repo allowlists and ignorelists.
Keep zombie PRs in low-touch mode unless new maintainer signal appears.
Replace repeated model-session quota probes with cheaper state checks when possible.
Use templated owner pings and comment dedupe; reserve model calls for nuanced reviewer replies.
Drop low-return repos after cheap bounty/review/merge signal checks.
Audit PR body links against closed issues before spending maintenance tokens.
Attempt external-repo privileged actions once; if permission is denied, record the boundary and stop retrying.
economic_strategy: Treat tokens as engineering capital, not free background fuel.
Watch many PRs with cheap metadata checks before launching full reasoning sessions.
Escalate only on failing CI, formal changes requested, merge conflicts, stale PR metadata, or maintainer feedback.
Separate payout eligibility from PR engineering value when bounty issues are closed.
Keep high-risk decisions, policy changes, and final approvals human-in-the-loop.
evolution_note: This policy evolved from Druid's own operating history: broad scans, zombie PR loops, repeated local maintenance candidates, and expensive quota probes were converted into pruning, dedupe, and stop-loss rules.
